label: Phone calls
rationale: One phone call on the noun denwa: calling, picking up and hanging up, then the phone ringing and calls that came in for you.
mixUps: The o/ni sets are things you do (kakeru, deru, kiru) and the ga sets happen to you (naru, aru, kakaru): denwa o kakeru vs denwa ga kakaru differ only in o/ga, with kara for the caller. This naru is 'ring', not naru 'become', and kiru ends the call.

targets.verbSense: hang or put something onto something; set something going (a call, a record)
targets.trap: Not yobu or iu: phoning someone is denwa o kakeru (or simply denwa suru); yobu is summon, iu is call something a name.
targets.use: Said when you phone someone, with the person marked by ni. For a plain 'I'll call you', denwa suru is the everyday default (ato de denwa suru ne); kakeru is what you hear for dialing and trying: kakete miru, nankai kakete mo denai (they don't pick up however many times I call). Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: kakenaosu = call again (after a dropped or missed call). The number takes ni: kono bangou ni kakete.

example.romaji: chotto okaasan ni denwa kakete miru.
example.ja: ちょっとお母さんに電話かけてみる。
example.english: Let me try calling my mom.

examplePolite.romaji: chotto haha ni denwa o kakete mimasu.
examplePolite.ja: ちょっと母に電話をかけてみます。
examplePolite.english: Let me try calling my mother.

targets.trap: Not denwa ni kotaeru: picking up is denwa ni deru ('come out to the phone'); kotaeru answers a question. denwa o toru (lift the receiver) is also natural, especially for office phones: denwa totte!
targets.use: Said about picking up, mostly in the negative: denwa denai (they're not picking up). Casual speech drops ni, and denwa dete means 'can you get the phone?'

example.romaji: zenzen denwa denai n da kedo.
example.ja: 全然電話出ないんだけど。
example.english: They're not picking up at all.

examplePolite.romaji: zenzen denwa ni denai n desu kedo.
examplePolite.ja: 全然電話に出ないんですけど。
examplePolite.english: They're not picking up at all.

targets.trap: Not kakeru ('hang'): denwa o kakeru makes the call; ending it is kiru ('cut').
targets.use: Said at the end of a call (jaa, kiru ne = OK, I'll hang up) and for being hung up on (kirareta). Casual speech drops o.
targets.notes: Not kiru 'wear' (fuku o kiru): a different verb with different pitch and conjugation. Hung up = kitta, kirimasu; wore = kita, kimasu. Intransitive: denwa ga kireta = the call cut off.

example.ja: ごめん、間違えて電話切っちゃった。
example.english: Sorry, I hung up by mistake.

examplePolite.ja: すみません、間違えて電話を切っちゃいました。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I hung up by mistake.

targets.verbSense: ring, sound (a phone, bell or alarm)
targets.trap: Spelled like naru 'become' and conjugated alike (natteru, natta), but the pitch differs: naru 'ring' is flat (na-RU), while naru 'become' falls after na (NA-ru). So keitai natteru yo means 'your phone's ringing'. Ringing something yourself is the transitive narasu (chaimu o narasu).
targets.use: Said as a heads-up when a phone rings, in the -teru form: denwa natteru yo (your phone's ringing), often just natteru yo. Casual speech drops ga. The past natta is for a ring that already happened: sakki denwa natta yo.
targets.notes: Alarms and stomachs use it too: mezamashi naranakatta (my alarm didn't go off), onaka natta (my stomach rumbled).

targets.english: (someone) called, there was a call from X
targets.trap: 'Your mom called' is okaasan kara denwa atta yo, with the caller marked by kara; okaasan ni denwa atta means a call came for her. okaasan ga denwa shita sounds like she called someone else.
targets.use: Said when passing on who called, in the past with the caller marked by kara: obaachan kara denwa atta yo (Grandma called). At work, passing on a call takes the polite odenwa: tanaka-san kara odenwa ga arimashita. Casual speech often drops ga.
targets.notes: denwa kakatte kita tells the call coming in to you; denwa atta reports that a call happened, often to pass it on. denwa kita is the casual short form, and renraku atta covers word by any channel.

example.romaji: tanaka-san kara denwa atta yo. orikaeshite hoshii tte.
example.ja: 田中さんから電話あったよ。折り返してほしいって。
example.english: Tanaka called. He wants you to call him back.

examplePolite.romaji: sakihodo tanaka-san kara odenwa ga arimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 先ほど田中さんからお電話がありました。

targets.verbSense: hang, be put onto; get going (the intransitive of kakeru)
targets.trap: Not okaasan kara denwa kaketa: kaketa says you made the call. An incoming call makes either the call the subject (okaasan kara denwa kakatte kita) or the caller the subject with -te kuru (okaasan ga denwa kakete kita). denwa kita and denwa moratta are also natural.
targets.use: Said of an incoming call, almost always as denwa kakatte kita (I got a call), with the caller marked by kara. The -te kuru shows the call coming toward you.
targets.notes: denwa kita is the short everyday version. Passing on a call that came while someone was out is denwa ga aru: tanaka-san kara denwa ga arimashita. This -te kuru means 'toward me', not the 'go and do' sense of -te kuru. The partners take kakaru in its 'running' sense.

example.romaji: sakki okaasan kara denwa kakatte kita.
example.ja: さっきお母さんから電話かかってきた。
example.english: My mom called a little while ago.

examplePolite.romaji: sakki haha kara denwa ga kakatte kimashita.
examplePolite.ja: さっき母から電話がかかってきました。
examplePolite.english: My mother called a little while ago.

reviewPool.english: suit someone, look good on someone
not suit someone, can't make it (a time)
